messages.content: Can you help me Get object descriptors related to a domain example.org on VirusTotal? The relationship I want to check is subdomains. You should just return the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any) instead of returning all attributes. My key is my_api. Set the limit to 10 and the continuation cursor to abc.

function.name: get_current_weather
function.description: Retrieves the current weather conditions for a specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to get the weather, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' if State for the city exists. 'City, Country' if State for the city doesn't exist.

unit.description: The unit of temperature for the weather report.

message.content:
Below is a minimal example of how you can query VirusTotal for the **subdomains** of `example.org` and then extract only the IDs (and any context attributes) from the response.

```bash
# Make the request
curl -s \
     -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/objects/domain/example.org/relationships?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc" \
     -H "x-apikey: my_api" \
     -o vt_response.json
```

Now parse the JSON to keep only the IDs (and any context attributes).  
If you’re using `jq`, this will give you a clean list:

```bash
cat vt_response.json | jq '.data[] | {id, type}'
```

### Expected shape of the output

```json
[
  {"id":"sub1.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub2.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub3.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub4.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub5.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub6.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub7.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub8.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub9.example.org","type":"domain"},
  {"id":"sub10.example.org","type":"domain"}
]
```

> **Note:**  
> * The exact IDs returned depend on the current data in VirusTotal.  
> * If there are more than 10 results, the `meta.continuation_cursor` field in the original response will contain a token you can use to fetch the next page.  

Feel free to adjust the `limit` or add additional filters (`filter[context_attributes]`) as needed.
